        ax.plot(range(15, 181, 15), [h["mae"] for h in result["per_horizon"]], label="Contextual LSTM 256")
        ax.set(xlabel="Forecast lead (assumed minutes)", ylabel="Test MAE", title="Frozen forecast errors by lead")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(output / "test_horizons.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)
        usable = [s["mae"] for s in result["per_sensor"] if s["mae"] is not None]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))

        fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(output / "sensor_errors.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)
        rows = "\n".join(f"| {row['model']} | {row['test']['mae']:.4f} | {row['test']['rmse']:.4f} | {row['test']['mape_percent']:.4f} |" for row in comparison)
        lead_rows = "\n".join(f"| {h['assumed_minutes']} | {h['mae']:.4f} | {h['rmse']:.4f} | {h['mape_percent']:.4f} |" for h in result["per_horizon"])
        lstm_mae = result["overall"]["mae"]
        patch_mae = patch["results"]["test"]["overall_pooled"]["mae"]
        relative_difference = 100 * (lstm_mae / patch_mae - 1)
        text = f'''# LSTM versus PatchSTG: project results
    
    ## Task and experimental decision
    
    Predict the next 12 traffic-flow readings from 12 historical readings on processed
    SD (716 sensors; assumed 15-minute cadence). LSTM applies the course method;
    PatchSTG is the previous project's spatial-attention adaptation. BigST and the
    unfinished width-384 LSTM are deferred by user decision to complete this scope.
    
    The original search planned widths 128/256/384. The user narrowed it to the two
    completed 50-epoch candidates before the contextual test pass. Width 256 won by
    best validation MAE, selecting epoch {selection['selected']['epoch']}. Width 384 is
    not a completed or rejected experiment; its existing artifacts are preserved.
    This is a revised two-candidate selection, not the original completed suite.
    
    ## Shared evaluation protocol
    
    Chronological train/validation/test boundaries are 21024/28032/35040. Training-only
    global normalization includes zeros. Targets remain in original units; zero
    targets are excluded, without imputation or prediction clipping. Score all 6,997
    test windows and {result['overall']['valid_targets']:,} included forecast-target
    pairs. Reference reports match data hashes, window protocol, and lead-wise counts.
    
    ## Test accuracy
    
    | Model | MAE | RMSE | MAPE (%) |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    {rows}
    
    Baseline/PatchSTG values are previous measured reports, not new executions.
    The contextual result is a new frozen evaluation on {result['device']}. The
    LSTM MAE is {relative_difference:+.2f}% relative to PatchSTG; negative means lower.
    This is a single-seed observed difference, not statistical significance.
    
    ## Learning and capacity
    
    ![Learning curves](learning_curves.png)
    
    The 128-unit candidate selected epoch 39 (validation MAE 15.3385); width 256
    selected epoch 37 (15.0656). Their final-epoch errors were higher than these
    best values, supporting validation checkpoint selection rather than automatically
    using epoch 50. Training scores pool changing weights, while validation scores
    use each completed epoch's frozen model. The plots should be read accordingly.
    
    Contextual LSTM has 848,644 parameters versus PatchSTG's 2,284,844. Relative to
    the small LSTM, context, layers and width changed together. Improved accuracy
    cannot identify the separate contribution of each change without ablations.
    
    ## Forecast distance
    
    ![Test MAE by forecast lead](test_horizons.png)
    
    | Assumed minutes ahead | LSTM MAE | LSTM RMSE | LSTM MAPE (%) |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    {lead_rows}
    
    Read the plotted curves to distinguish near-term behavior from long-lead errors.
    A pooled score can conceal such differences. Longer-lead error is consistent
    with less immediate observational guidance, but this experiment alone does not
    establish its cause or prove spatial attention is responsible for a difference.
    
    ## Sensor variation and data coverage
    
    ![Selected LSTM sensor errors](sensor_errors.png)
    
    {len(usable)} sensors have included test targets; {716-len(usable)} have none and
    are explicitly assigned null metrics in report.json. Error variation among
    scored sensors motivates sensor-level interpretation, but the distribution is
    for LSTM only: reference reports do not provide matching per-sensor forecasts.
    Do not claim a spatial explanation from this histogram alone. Zeros may indicate
    missingness or true zero flow; masking is a benchmark convention.
    
    ## Fairness, interpretation, and limitations
    
    Both contextual LSTM and PatchSTG use traffic, calendar and learned sensor identity.
    The LSTM processes sensors independently. PatchSTG additionally uses coordinates,
    training-derived similarity, and spatial attention. PatchSTG uses AdamW with
    different learning rate, schedule, decay and clipping; LSTM uses fixed-lr Adam.
    Matching 50 epochs aligns dataset passes, not computation or tuning budget.
    The LSTM search used two completed widths; report that extra selection effort.

    full-paper reproduction. Only one seed and one network were studied. There is

    Previous-project and small-LSTM test results were already observed before this
    follow-up design; the test set is reused rather than newly unseen. No test score
    selected this contextual checkpoint and no further tuning follows this test pass.
    
    Calendar timestamps and metadata/sensor pairing remain assumptions. Timing is
    recorded in run reports but is not a controlled comparison of inference kernels.
    Historical PatchSTG reports were validated structurally; this run does not
    reproduce its forward predictions or independently re-establish its source data.
    
    ## Reproduction and artifacts
    
    - selection.json: frozen validation-only choice and explicit scope revision.
    - report.json: frozen LSTM test metrics, horizons, sensors, identity and checks.
    - comparison.json: reference report paths/hashes and overall metrics.
    - Figures above: generated from stored learning histories and measured scores.
    
    Run from the project root with a new output directory:
    
    ```bash
    python finalize_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output-dir runs/final_comparison_v1
    ```
    
    The script refuses existing outputs, creates no optimizer, uses no-grad scoring,
    and checks model tensors and checkpoint bytes remain unchanged. Existing training
    code, reports and checkpoints are not modified. Final test results are fixed.

    def main():
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("--suite", type=Path, default=root / "runs/context_lstm_suite_v1")
        parser.add_argument("--previous-project", type=Path, default=root.parent / "Practical ML Project")
        parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=root / "runs/final_comparison_v1")
        parser.add_argument("--device", choices=("cpu", "cuda"), default="cuda")
        parser.add_argument("--prepare-only", action="store_true", help="Freeze selection and check identity; no forward passes or test scoring.")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if args.output_dir.exists():
            raise FileExistsError("Choose a new directory; previous results are preserved.")
        # Preparation can run on CPU without requiring a GPU in the agent environment.
        setup("cpu" if args.prepare_only else args.device)
        selection = select_completed(args.suite, root)
        checkpoint = torch.load(selection["selected"]["checkpoint"], map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        metadata = checkpoint["metadata"]
        data_path = root / "data/raw/largest_sd/flowsd.npz"
        if sha256(data_path) != metadata["data_sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Data hash differs from training.")
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        (args.output_dir / "selection.json").write_text(json.dumps(selection, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(f"Frozen selection: hidden {checkpoint['hidden_size']}, epoch {checkpoint['epoch']}; width 384 deferred.", flush=True)
        if args.prepare_only:
            print("Preparation complete; no validation or test predictions evaluated.")
            return
        traffic = load_traffic(data_path)
        train_end, test_start = split_boundaries(len(traffic))
        mean, std = fit_normalization(traffic[:train_end])
        if metadata["scaler"] != {"mean": float(mean), "std": float(std)}:
            raise ValueError("Training normalization differs.")
        if metadata["splits"] != {"train": [0, train_end], "validation": [train_end, test_start]}:
            raise ValueError("Split boundaries differ.")
        model = ContextLSTM(mean, std, hidden_size=checkpoint["hidden_size"]).to(args.device)
        model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state"], strict=True)
        original = {name: value.detach().cpu().clone() for name, value in model.state_dict().items()}
        val_loader = DataLoader(TrafficDataset(traffic, (train_end, test_start), mean, std), batch_size=4, shuffle=False)
        print("Checking complete frozen validation...", flush=True)
        validation = run_epoch(model, val_loader)
        for metric in ("mae", "rmse", "mape_percent"):
            if not math.isclose(validation[metric], checkpoint["validation"][metric], rel_tol=1e-5, abs_tol=1e-4):
                raise ValueError("Validation reproduction failed; test not evaluated.")
        if validation["valid_targets"] != 58367674 or validation["windows"] != 6997:
            raise ValueError("Validation coverage differs.")
        print("Validation reproduced. Evaluating frozen test set...", flush=True)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        test_loader = DataLoader(TrafficDataset(traffic, (test_start, len(traffic)), mean, std), batch_size=4, shuffle=False)
        result = score_frozen(model, test_loader)
        result["scoring_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - start
        if result["windows"] != 6997 or result["overall"]["valid_targets"] != 58158396:
            raise ValueError("Incomplete test coverage.")
        starts = range(test_start, len(traffic) - model.horizon + 1)
        for lead, metrics in enumerate(result["per_horizon"]):
            if np.count_nonzero(traffic[starts.start + lead:starts.stop + lead]) != metrics["valid_targets"]:
                raise ValueError("Per-lead mask count mismatch.")
        for name, value in model.state_dict().items():
            torch.testing.assert_close(value.cpu(), original[name], rtol=0, atol=0)
        if any(p.grad is not None for p in model.parameters()):
            raise RuntimeError("Unexpected parameter gradients.")
        path = Path(selection["selected"]["checkpoint"])
        if sha256(path) != selection["selected"]["checkpoint_sha256"]:
            raise RuntimeError("Checkpoint bytes changed.")
        result.update(status="complete", hidden_size=checkpoint["hidden_size"], selected_epoch=checkpoint["epoch"],
                      device=args.device, scaler=metadata["scaler"], data_sha256=metadata["data_sha256"],
                      checkpoint_sha256=sha256(path), model_state_unchanged=True, checkpoint_unchanged=True,
                      evaluation_source_sha256=sha256(Path(__file__).resolve()), validation_recheck=validation,
                      torch=str(torch.__version__), numpy=np.__version__, test_target_interval=[test_start, len(traffic)],
                      batch_size=4, precision=metadata["precision"], training_metadata=metadata)
        (args.output_dir / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(result["overall"], indent=2), flush=True)
        build_comparison(args.output_dir, selection, result, args.previous_project, root)
        print("Complete. Read:", args.output_dir / "PROJECT_REPORT.md", flush=True)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    # Implementation: finalize_context_lstm.py
    
    Source: [finalize_context_lstm.py](../../finalize_context_lstm.py).
    
    This completes the reduced two-candidate project scope without training width
    384. It preserves the original suite/checkpoints and writes a separate frozen
    evaluation directory, not a misleading completed three-width suite summary.
    
    ## Functions
    
    - `select_completed`: verify completed 128/256 training reports, checkpoint
      selection, metadata, source identities and coverage. Select lowest validation
      MAE and freeze a manifest. No test scores participate. Width 384 is deferred.
    - `metric_values`: derive pooled MAE/RMSE/MAPE or null values for zero coverage.
    - `score_frozen`: eval/no-grad contextual forecasts, with historical calendar,
      pooling overall, per-horizon and per-sensor errors without storing all forecasts.
    - `check_reference`: require matching previous PatchSTG data/scaler/windows and
      lead-wise target counts before comparison.
    - `build_comparison`: verify old reference reports and PatchSTG checkpoint hash,
      generate learning curves, lead curves, sensor-error distribution, machine-readable
      comparison and an interpreted Markdown project report. Old reference values
      are explicitly historical; no new PatchSTG inference is claimed.
    - `main`: verify paths/data/scaler/splits, reproduce selected validation, run test,
      independently count masks, assert frozen model/checkpoint integrity, and write.
    
    ## Execution
    
    ```bash
    python -u finalize_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output-dir runs/final_comparison_v1
    ```
    
    The directory must not exist. `--prepare-only` can freeze and check selection
    without GPU access or any forward passes, using a separate output directory.
    The agent executed that preparation in reports/context_lstm_final_selection_v1.
    
    Validation tolerates small CPU/GPU metric differences (rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-4),
    while window/mask counts match exactly. No optimizer or gradients are created.
    Mean/std, weights and checkpoint bytes remain unchanged. Global/matmul/cuDNN
    RNN precision uses the contextual runner's explicit IEEE settings.
    
    ## Interpretation limits
    
    Only the two completed candidates participate. The scope revision occurred after
    interim validation observations; it must be disclosed. Previously observed test
    results and unequal capacity/input/optimizer/search budgets remain limitations.
    Per-sensor analysis is LSTM-only because old reports lack paired sensor-level
    forecasts. Do not infer a spatial causal explanation from those figures.
    
    Actual test output is pending host execution; synthetic metric and temporary
    report-generation checks have passed. See
    [finalization status](../../reports/finalization_status.md).

    # Reduced project scope and frozen LSTM selection
    
    The user explicitly deferred the unfinished 384-unit candidate to finish the
    project. Its checkpoints and partial results are preserved. It is not a completed
    candidate, and the original three-width suite is not relabeled complete.
    
    Selection is now among the two completed 50-epoch candidates, by lowest best
    full-validation MAE:
    
    | Width | Parameters | Best epoch | Validation MAE |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | 128 | 234,244 | 39 | 15.3385 |
    | **256** | **848,644** | **37** | **15.0656** |
    
    Frozen manifest: [selection.json](context_lstm_final_selection_v1/selection.json).
    Both report/checkpoint pairs, all 50 epoch records, source hashes, and dataset
    identity were checked. No contextual test prediction was calculated during
    selection/preparation. The decision followed observation of interim validation
    results, including partial width-384 results; disclose this scope revision.
    
    ## Finishing command
    
    Stop any existing contextual suite process first, in the terminal that can see it:
    
    ```bash
    pkill -TERM -f '^python -u train_context_lstm.py'
    ```
    
    Then run the frozen evaluation/report builder on the user's GPU:
    
    ```bash
    python -u finalize_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output-dir runs/final_comparison_v1
    ```
    
    This verifies full validation, evaluates the selected test checkpoint without
    updates, checks frozen-state/coverage integrity, and generates overall,
    per-horizon and per-sensor LSTM metrics plus comparison figures/report.
    It reads historical baseline/PatchSTG reports and verifies matching data/protocol/
    coverage; it also verifies the previous PatchSTG checkpoint's recorded hash.

    """Resolve the project and preserve pre-cleanup source identities."""
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    
    
    def recorded_source_path(root, recorded_name):
        """Locate exact code bytes referenced by historical checkpoint metadata.
    
        Old checkpoints name root-level scripts. Their immutable snapshots preserve
        those hashes after relocation/import changes. New checkpoints use explicit
        src/ paths. This verifies historical identity, not equality of migrated code;
        migration records and evaluation reports identify current execution sources.
        """
        current = root / recorded_name
        if current.is_file():
            return current
        historical = root / "reproducibility" / "original_sources" / recorded_name
        if historical.is_file():
            return historical
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Recorded source not found: {recorded_name}")

        from pathlib import Path
        import json,shutil
        root=Path.cwd();p=root/'reproducibility/path_migration.json';moves=json.loads(p.read_text())
        for directory in (root/'runs').iterdir():
         if not directory.is_dir() or directory.name.startswith(('context_lstm_suite','final_comparison')): continue
         dest=root/'temp/experiments'/directory.name;dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
         # Map each file as well as the directory so historical Markdown links resolve.
         for child in directory.rglob('*'):
          moves[str(child.relative_to(root))]=str((dest/child.relative_to(directory)).relative_to(root))
         moves[str(directory.relative_to(root))]=str(dest.relative_to(root))
         shutil.move(str(directory),dest)
        p.write_text(json.dumps(moves,indent=2)+'\n')
        # Rewrite Markdown targets according to where they pointed BEFORE relocation.
        # Reports/checkpoint JSON bytes are deliberately never rewritten.
        inverse={v:k for k,v in moves.items()}
        import re,os
        for doc in list(root.rglob('*.md')):
         if any(part in {'.git','original_sources','reference_project','data'} for part in doc.relative_to(root).parts):continue
         rel=str(doc.relative_to(root)); old=root/inverse.get(rel,rel)
         text=doc.read_text()
         def relocate(match):
          target=match.group(1)
          if target.startswith(('https://','http://','#')):return match.group(0)
          body,sep,anchor=target.partition('#')
          old_target=Path(os.path.normpath(old.parent/body))
          try:old_rel=str(old_target.relative_to(root))
          except ValueError:return match.group(0)
          new_target=root/moves.get(old_rel,old_rel)
          new_path=os.path.relpath(new_target,doc.parent)
          return ']('+new_path+(sep+anchor if sep else '')+')'
         text=re.sub(r'\]\(([^)]+)\)',relocate,text)
         # Only update runnable active command names, not historical inactive snippets.
         for command in ('audit_data','inspect_data','check_context_lstm','check_context_training','train_context_lstm','finalize_context_lstm'):
          text=text.replace('python -u '+command+'.py','python -u scripts/'+command+'.py')
          text=text.replace('python '+command+'.py','python scripts/'+command+'.py')
         doc.write_text(text)
        print('Archived old small-LSTM/interrupted runs; updated Markdown links and active command paths.')

    # Traffic forecasting: contextual LSTM versus PatchSTG
    
    Course project using processed SD traffic observations. The selected contextual
    LSTM has two layers, 256 hidden units, calendar/sensor embeddings, and 848,644
    parameters. It was selected at epoch 37 using validation MAE 15.0656 from the
    two completed 50-epoch candidates. The unfinished 384-unit run is deferred.
    
    ## Project layout
    
    ```text
    README.md                 Start here
    guide.md                  Step-by-step reading path
    src/traffic_prediction/   Data, models, metrics, training and evaluation code
    scripts/                  Runnable commands
    docs/                     Concept guides and implementation walkthroughs
    reports/                  Audit, experiment decisions and recorded checks
    runs/                     Current candidate checkpoints and generated final results
    data/raw/largest_sd/      Local traffic array and metadata
    reproducibility/          Original source snapshots and historical reference evidence
    temp/                    Archived notes, scripts, logs and superseded experiments
    ```
    
    Nothing was deleted during cleanup. `temp/` is not part of the main submission
    narrative; it keeps earlier educational work recoverable. Keep `reproducibility/`:
    existing checkpoints reference original source hashes, and the selected evaluator
    checks them against those exact archived bytes. Current execution source hashes
    are separately recorded in the new evaluation report.
    
    ## Run the selected evaluation and comparison
    
    Use the existing environment from the project root:
    
    ```bash
    conda activate pml
    python -u scripts/finalize_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output-dir runs/final_comparison_v1
    ```
    
    The output directory must be new. This checks the selected checkpoint, reproduces
    validation, scores frozen test predictions, and writes:
    
    - `PROJECT_REPORT.md`: comparison, interpretation, and limitations.
    - `report.json`, `selection.json`, `comparison.json`: machine-readable evidence.
    - Learning curves, forecast-lead curves, and a sensor-error distribution.
    
    Final contextual test scoring has been prepared, not yet recorded as completed
    at cleanup time. Baseline and PatchSTG test values are historical measured
    reference reports bundled locally; the command does not retrain PatchSTG.
    It no longer needs the neighboring project folder.
    
    ## Checks and learning
    
    ```bash
    python scripts/check_context_training.py
    python scripts/inspect_data.py
    ```
    
    The first is a synthetic training/validation/resume check. The second runs the
    data walkthrough and baseline validation; neither starts a long training suite.
    
    For GPU feasibility on a new report path:
    
    ```bash
    python scripts/check_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output reports/gpu_probe_repeat.json
    ```
    
    Start learning with [guide.md](guide.md), then use [the documentation index](docs/README.md).

    # Clean project structure and migration
    
    Cleanup groups code and separates current work from development history. It
    does not change the LSTM architecture, learned weights, data splits, masks,
    normalization or existing scores. Existing checkpoint/report JSON files are
    preserved byte-for-byte; their embedded original paths remain historical records.
    
    ## Where files moved
    
    | Previous location/type | Current location |
    | --- | --- |
    | Reusable root Python modules | `src/traffic_prediction/` |
    | Main runnable tools | `scripts/` entry points |
    | Old root learning/decision notes | `temp/notes/` |
    | Original small-LSTM-only diagnostic/evaluation scripts | `temp/legacy_scripts/` |
    | Earlier small-model/interrupted run folders | `temp/experiments/` |
    | Old terminal logs | `temp/logs/` |
    | Superseded CPU feasibility reports | `temp/diagnostic_reports/` |
    | Exact original root sources | `reproducibility/original_sources/` |
    | Historical baseline/PatchSTG evidence | `reproducibility/reference_project/` |
    
    The current contextual suite stays under runs/context_lstm_suite_v1. Its deferred
    384 artifacts are retained in place, so cleanup does not discard or relabel the
    incomplete experiment. No source data/checkpoint was deleted.
    
    ## Commands and imports
    
    Use `python scripts/NAME.py`, not the former root command. Each small entry point
    adds src/ to the Python path and calls its package module's main function.
    The package uses relative imports. A shared paths module resolves the project
    root from the package location; data/report paths do not accidentally point inside src/.
    
    Do not run the archived scripts directly as current entry points. They are exact
    historical copies, not adapted executable tools. Some small-model training modules
    remain in the package because other modules reuse their serialization, validation
    or hash helpers; they are support code, not the recommended final experiment.
    
    ## Source hashes after a layout change
    
    Original training records contain root-level source names and hashes. Relocation
    requires import/path updates, so current file bytes differ. The original snapshots
    and original_sources.json preserve the measured experiment's code identity.
    recorded_source_path resolves old names to those snapshots; new runs record src/
    paths. The frozen evaluator verifies the originals and records hashes of current
    runtime modules separately. This does not pretend migrated bytes are unchanged.
    
    path_migration.json lists old/new locations. These records support provenance and
    recovery; they do not rewrite previously saved experimental evidence.
    
    For an explicitly authorized return to the original three-candidate suite, the
    migrated trainer supports existing suite metadata while checking original source
    identities and unchanged settings. The current scope still defers 384; cleanup
    does not restart it. CPU regression checks and frozen-selection checks are used
    to verify migration without launching long training or test evaluation.
    
    ## Bundled reference evidence
    
    The selected report builder uses local copies of previous baseline/PatchSTG
    JSON reports and the matching PatchSTG checkpoint to verify its recorded hash.
    No previous-project directory is required. The PatchSTG result is historical,
    not a new forward pass; attribution and implementation limitations remain in
    the reports. These reference artifacts are not the new contextual LSTM weights.
    
    See [README](../README.md) for submission/runtime asset requirements.

    """Evaluate a frozen validation-selected PatchSTG checkpoint on the full SD test split."""
    
    import argparse
    from dataclasses import asdict
    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import platform
    import subprocess
    
    os.environ.setdefault('CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG', ':4096:8')
    
    import numpy as np
    import torch
    from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
    
    from traffic_benchmark.data import GlobalStandardScaler, TrafficWindows, load_processed_sd, make_splits
    from traffic_benchmark.data.spatial import load_spatial_maps
    from traffic_benchmark.evaluation.checkpoint import file_sha256, validate_checkpoint, restore_frozen_model
    from traffic_benchmark.training.trainer import evaluate, seed_everything
    
    
    def git_output(*args):
        try:
            return subprocess.check_output(['git', *args], text=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()
        except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            return None
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument('--run-dir', type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
        parser.add_argument('--data-dir', type=Path, default=Path('data/raw/largest_sd'))
        parser.add_argument('--device', choices=('cpu', 'cuda:0'), default='cuda:0')
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if args.output.exists():
            parser.error('Output exists; choose a new path. Do not overwrite test results.')
        if args.device == 'cuda:0' and not torch.cuda.is_available():
            parser.error('CUDA unavailable; no automatic CPU fallback.')
        report = json.loads((args.run_dir / 'report.json').read_text())
        checkpoint_path = args.run_dir / 'best.pt'
        checkpoint_hash = file_sha256(checkpoint_path)
        checkpoint = torch.load(checkpoint_path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=True)
        values, _ = load_processed_sd(args.data_dir)
        splits = make_splits(len(values))
        scaler = GlobalStandardScaler.fit(values, splits['train'][1])
        hashes = {name: file_sha256(args.data_dir / name) for name in ('flowsd.npz', 'sd_meta.csv')}
        identity = validate_checkpoint(checkpoint, report, hashes, splits, scaler)
        config = identity['model_config']
        if config['nodes'] != 716 or config['history'] != 12 or config['slots_per_day'] != 96:
            raise ValueError('Expected fixed SD 716-node, 12-to-12, 15-minute protocol.')
        seed = report['config']['seed']
        torch.set_num_threads(2)
        seed_everything(seed)
        maps = load_spatial_maps(args.run_dir / 'spatial_maps.npz', identity['spatial'])
        model = restore_frozen_model(checkpoint, maps).to(args.device)
        dataset = TrafficWindows(values, splits['test'], scaler)
        batch_size = report['config']['batch_size']
        loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=0)
        if args.device == 'cuda:0':
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
        result = evaluate(model, loader, scaler, torch.device(args.device), 12)
        if result['windows'] != len(dataset):
            raise ValueError('Incomplete test evaluation.')
        result['per_horizon'] = [{**row, 'minutes': row['step'] * 15} for row in result['per_horizon']]
        output = {
            'status': 'completed', 'model': 'PatchSTG',
            'implementation': 'code-aligned shared-protocol adaptation; not an official reproduction',
            'created_utc': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            'checkpoint': {'path': str(checkpoint_path), 'sha256': checkpoint_hash,
                           'epoch': checkpoint['epoch'], 'validation_mae': checkpoint['validation_mae'],
                           'selection': 'lowest full validation pooled MAE; first epoch wins ties'},
            'training_report_sha256': file_sha256(args.run_dir / 'report.json'),
            'spatial_maps_sha256': file_sha256(args.run_dir / 'spatial_maps.npz'),
            'training_identity': identity, 'seed': seed, 'scaler': asdict(scaler),
            'config': {'split': 'test', 'splits': splits, 'history': 12, 'horizon': 12,
                       'stride': 1, 'batch_size': batch_size, 'shuffle': False, 'num_workers': 0,
                       'device': args.device, 'precision': identity['precision'],
                       'target_mask': 'nonzero targets only; no clipping; MAPE percent without epsilon',
                       'prediction_units': 'original flow units', 'test_used_for_tuning': False},
            'source_hashes': hashes,
            'software': {'python': platform.python_version(), 'torch': str(torch.__version__),
                         'numpy': np.__version__, 'cuda_build': torch.version.cuda,
                         'cudnn': torch.backends.cudnn.version()},
            'hardware': {'platform': platform.platform(), 'processor': platform.processor()},
            'git': {'revision': git_output('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), 'status': git_output('status', '--porcelain')},
            'implementation_hashes': {p: file_sha256(p) for p in (
                'scripts/evaluate_patchstg.py', 'src/traffic_benchmark/evaluation/checkpoint.py')},
            'parameters': sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()),
            'results': {'test': result},
            'timing_scope': 'Single full test pass: loading batches, transfers, forward, inverse scaling, metrics; '
                            'excludes setup; no warmup; not an isolated inference-speed benchmark',
        }
        if args.device == 'cuda:0':
            props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
            output['hardware']['gpu'] = {'name': props.name, 'total_memory_bytes': props.total_memory,
                                        'compute_capability': list(torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0))}
            output['peak_allocated_bytes'] = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()
            output['peak_reserved_bytes'] = torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved()
        # Verify originals remained unchanged throughout inference.
        if file_sha256(checkpoint_path) != checkpoint_hash:
            raise ValueError('Checkpoint changed during evaluation.')
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with args.output.open('x') as stream:
            json.dump(output, stream, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
            stream.write('\n')
        print('Test:', json.dumps(result['overall_pooled']))
        print('Saved', args.output)
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        raise SystemExit(main())
    """Integrity checks for frozen, validation-selected PatchSTG checkpoints."""
    
    import hashlib
    import json
    from dataclasses import asdict
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import numpy as np
    import torch
    
    from traffic_benchmark.models import PatchSTG, PatchSTGConfig
    
    
    def file_sha256(path):
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        with Path(path).open('rb') as stream:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
                digest.update(chunk)
        return digest.hexdigest()
    
    
    def canonical(value):
        return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False)
    
    
    def validate_checkpoint(checkpoint, report, source_hashes, splits, scaler):
        """Fail closed on diagnostic runs, stale inputs/code, or wrong selection."""
        if (report.get('status') != 'completed' or report.get('diagnostic_subset') is not False
                or not report.get('history')):
            raise ValueError('A completed full-split training run is required.')
        if checkpoint.get('kind') != 'best':
            raise ValueError('Test evaluation requires the best checkpoint.')
        identity = report['identity']
        if canonical(checkpoint['identity']) != canonical(identity):
            raise ValueError('Checkpoint and training report identities differ.')
        selected = min(report['history'], key=lambda row: row['validation']['overall_pooled']['mae'])
        score = selected['validation']['overall_pooled']['mae']
        if (checkpoint['epoch'] != selected['epoch'] or report['best_epoch'] != selected['epoch']
                or checkpoint['validation_mae'] != score or report['best_validation_mae'] != score):
            raise ValueError('Checkpoint does not match validation-only best selection.')
        if canonical(identity['source_sha256']) != canonical(source_hashes):
            raise ValueError('Dataset checksums differ from training.')
        if canonical(identity['splits']) != canonical(splits):
            raise ValueError('Split boundaries differ from training.')
        if checkpoint['scaler'] != asdict(scaler) or identity['scaler'] != asdict(scaler):
            raise ValueError('Training-only scaler differs from checkpoint.')
        if identity['spatial']['source_sha256'] != source_hashes or identity['spatial']['scaler'] != asdict(scaler):
            raise ValueError('Spatial preprocessing identity differs from dataset/scaler.')
        for path, expected in identity['implementation_sha256'].items():
            if file_sha256(path) != expected:
                raise ValueError(f'Training implementation changed: {path}')
        return identity
    
    
    def restore_frozen_model(checkpoint, maps):
        """Check spatial buffers before strict loading; loading would overwrite them."""
        state = checkpoint['model']
        for name, expected in (('gather_indices', maps.gather), ('restore_indices', maps.restore)):
            actual = state[name]
            if actual.dtype != torch.long or not np.array_equal(actual.cpu().numpy(), expected):
                raise ValueError(f'Checkpoint spatial buffer mismatch: {name}')
        model = PatchSTG(PatchSTGConfig(**checkpoint['identity']['model_config']), maps)
        model.load_state_dict(state, strict=True)
        if any(not torch.isfinite(value).all() for value in model.parameters()):
            raise ValueError('Nonfinite checkpoint parameters.')
        model.requires_grad_(False)
        return model.eval()

    """Research framework for comparative traffic forecasting experiments."""
    """Small, explicit contracts for chronological historical forecast replay."""
    
    import json
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta
    
    import numpy as np
    
    
    def select_windows(dataset, start_window=0, frames=96, frame_stride=1):
        """Select by chronological index only, never forecast error or target values."""
        for name, value in (('start_window', start_window), ('frames', frames), ('frame_stride', frame_stride)):
            if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or value < (0 if name == 'start_window' else 1):
                raise ValueError(f'Invalid {name}.')
        indices = list(range(start_window, start_window + frames * frame_stride, frame_stride))
        if indices[-1] >= len(dataset):
            raise ValueError('Requested replay extends beyond eligible test windows.')
        return indices
    
    
    def replay_payload(values, metadata, dataset, indices, predictions, provenance):
        """Store contiguous raw observations plus (frame,sensor,lead) predictions.
    
        Prediction input shape is (frames,horizon,sensors,1), in original units.
        Only exported predictions are rounded (3 decimals); benchmark reports stay exact.
        """
        if not indices or any(b <= a for a, b in zip(indices, indices[1:])):
            raise ValueError('Replay indices must be nonempty and strictly chronological.')
        if indices[0] < 0 or indices[-1] >= len(dataset):
            raise ValueError('Replay index outside dataset.')
        starts = [dataset.target_starts[i] for i in indices]
        horizon, history, nodes = dataset.horizon, dataset.history, values.shape[1]
        predictions = np.asarray(predictions)
        if predictions.shape != (len(indices), horizon, nodes, 1) or not np.isfinite(predictions).all():
            raise ValueError('Expected finite (frames,horizon,sensors,1) predictions.')
        if len(metadata) != nodes:
            raise ValueError('Sensor metadata count mismatch.')
        base = starts[0] - history
        stop = starts[-1] + horizon
        observations = values[base:stop, :, 0]

    # PatchSTG architecture review
    
    Reviewed 2026-11-11. Subsequent approved implementation and CPU checks complete;
    see [implementation record](../patchstg_implementation.md). No training yet.
    Target: adapted SD evaluation, not an official reproduction.
    
    ## Intuition and paper mapping
    
    PatchSTG reduces the number of sensor pairs involved in spatial attention by
    organizing sensors into balanced spatial patches. Paper sections 4.1–4.4 map to
    embedding, irregular spatial patching, dual attention and prediction projection.
    Spatial organization preserves individual sensor representations rather than
    replacing each patch with one pooled token. See [paper v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.09972v2).
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        A[Traffic and input calendar] --> B[Embedding]
        C[Coordinates and training similarity] --> D[Patch index maps]
        B --> E[Reorder and pad]
        D --> E
        E --> F[Depth and breadth attention]
        F --> G[Restore sensor order]
        G --> H[Forecast projection]
    ```
    
    ## Concrete SD reference and shapes
    
    The [pinned SD config](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/blob/8b298b230227a304a082e05241c69dca3740a73d/config/SD.conf)
    uses H=F=12, temporal patch size 12, one temporal patch, five layers, and embedding
    widths 64/64/32/32 for signal/node/day-slot/weekday. Total D=192. Leaf depth 9,
    capacity 2, merge factor 32 imply 512 leaves, 1,024 padded positions, P=16 merged
    patches and S=64 positions per patch. Batch 16 and 50 epochs are author settings,
    not promises for our GPU or a frozen project training budget.
    
    Following the [model reference](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/blob/8b298b230227a304a082e05241c69dca3740a73d/models/model.py):
    
    | Stage | Shape |
    | --- | --- |
    | Traffic; expanded integer calendar | (B,12,716,1); (B,12,716,2) |
    | Temporal signal projection plus embeddings | (B,1,716,192) |
    | Gather and reshape | (B,1,16,64,192) |
    | Depth attention sequence / breadth sequence | 64 positions / 16 patches |
    | Restore original sensors; decode | (B,1,716,192) → (B,12,716,1) |
    
    Each block uses one attention head, pre-normalization, residual connections,
    GELU MLPs with width ratio 1, and 0.1 attention/projection/MLP dropout. The signal
    projection also consumes normalized calendar scalars. Output is normalized flow;
    our adapter should invert the scaler before original-unit loss/evaluation.
    No future traffic or future calendar is required by this forward path.
    
    ## Spatial preparation and discrepancy
    
    The [pinned utilities](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/blob/8b298b230227a304a082e05241c69dca3740a73d/lib/utils.py)
    recursively split coordinates, pad leaves using similarity, and produce gather/
    restore maps. Similarity comes from mean normalized training segments and cosine
    similarity, followed by an exponential transform. The segment length is hard-coded
    to 288; at SD cadence that is three days, not one day. For exact code behavior,
    21024 training frames provide 73 full segments. A cadence-aware 96-step profile
    would be a deliberate adaptation, not a silent correction.
    
    Recommendation for the first reference-aligned implementation: preserve the
    288-step behavior and label it. Use explicit training-only inputs and new,
    provenance-checked cache identity. Test zero norms, zero similarity variance,
    index uniqueness/restoration and deterministic tie handling before trusting maps.
    No maps were generated during the review; the subsequent approved implementation
    now builds provenance-checked maps as recorded in the implementation guide.
    
    ## Fidelity and implementation choices
    
    The paper's SD embedding dimensions differ from the config. Use the config as
    the initial code-aligned architecture and record the discrepancy; do not claim
    paper-exact dimensions. The author training entry point inverse-transforms output
    and uses AdamW; its scheduler milestones differ in wording from the paper.
    See [main.py](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/blob/main/main.py).
    
    The subsequent implementation uses ordinary PyTorch attention/MLP components
    with fixed-weight numerical checks, avoiding a timm dependency. This is an independently written
    adapted implementation. Preserve checkpoint behavior, dropout and normalization
    semantics; test CPU/CUDA index buffers and state-dict round trips.
    
    PatchSTG's [software license](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/blob/main/LICENSE)
    is MIT, copyright 2024 LMissher. Any copied/adapted source must retain its notices.
    Dataset terms are a separate unresolved issue. See [implementation plan](../model_implementation_plan.md).
    # PatchSTG training harness
    
    Current status (November 13): 50-total-epoch seed-2023 training is complete.
    Best epoch 50 has validation MAE 14.9936. Frozen test evaluation is also complete:
    MAE 17.1943, RMSE 29.1370, MAPE 11.1706%. See
    [test results](../reports/patchstg_sd_seed2023_test_v1.md) and
    [evaluation command](patchstg_evaluation.md). Earlier diagnostic/calibration
    sections below are historical; pending-launch statements are superseded.
    
    
    Implemented November 12, 2026. Harness tests and a two-batch real-data CPU
    diagnostic passed. Host GPU capped training diagnostic also passed; see
    [measured diagnostic](../reports/patchstg_training_smoke_host.md). This is not a
    completed accuracy experiment or a reproduction of published PatchSTG results.
    
    ## Run the approved short diagnostic
    
    From the project root in your own WSL terminal:
    
    ```bash
    conda activate pml
    PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/train_patchstg.py --config configs/patchstg_smoke.json --output-dir runs/patchstg_train_smoke_host_v1
    ```
    
    The JSON configuration caps execution at **one diagnostic epoch, 20 training
    batches and 20 validation batches**, batch 4, seed 2023. This samples at most 80
    training and 80 validation windows. It does not process full epochs and never
    evaluates test data. New output directories are required; CUDA unavailability
    exits 2 with a report, without silently using CPU. Optional --cache accepts an
    existing provenance-matching spatial cache; otherwise maps are reconstructed.
    
    Share the epoch summary or report.json after the host run. We will use actual
    post-warm-up step timings to plan the next experiment. No full-run configuration
    or automatic final experiment is supplied by this milestone.
    
    ## Training and validation rules
    
    | Component | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Architecture | Existing full-width SD PatchSTG; config defaults resolved into artifacts |
    | Input | Existing normalized x and assumed input calendar; training data only for updates |
    | Targets | Original flow units; never inverse-transform targets a second time |
    | Loss | Inverse-transform model outputs, then mean absolute error on nonzero targets |
    | Empty training mask | Clear gradients and skip update, including AdamW weight decay; count skips |
    | Invalid numeric values | Fail on nonfinite predictions, targets, loss, gradients or updated weights |
    | Optimizer | AdamW, lr 0.002, weight decay 0.0001, foreach=False |
    | Gradient clipping | Global gradient norm 5, rejecting nonfinite norms |
    | Scheduler | Epoch-end MultiStepLR at 1,35,40, gamma 0.5, after validation |
    | Selection | Lowest pooled validation MAE; ties keep the earlier best |
    | Metrics | Shared original-unit MAE/RMSE/percentage MAPE and valid-target counts |
    | Train ordering | Seeded shuffled windows; num_workers=0; incomplete final batch retained |
    | Validation ordering | Sequential windows; no gradient recording, parameter updates or shuffling |
    | Precision | FP32; deterministic algorithms, TF32/cuDNN benchmark disabled; no AMP/compilation |
    
    Optimizer, clipping and scheduler settings follow the reviewed
    [pinned author entry point](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/blob/8b298b230227a304a082e05241c69dca3740a73d/main.py).
    The diagnostic caps, shared split/calendar rules, explicit empty-mask handling,
    pooled training logging and foreach=False are project choices. No author training
    runner was copied. The first epoch uses lr 0.002; with this schedule the second
    uses 0.001. Changing epoch caps to final experiment settings requires a reviewed
    configuration and separate experiment approval, not an undocumented edit.
    
    Training MAE is accumulated with valid-count weighting while parameters change
    across updates. It is an online training diagnostic, not a fixed-model training-set
    evaluation. Validation MAE pools all evaluated valid targets using the existing
    metric accumulator. An entirely invalid training epoch or validation subset fails
    rather than producing zero loss or selecting a checkpoint. Limits are implemented
    without fetching an extra batch beyond the requested cap.

    """Convenient entry point for integrated PatchSTG tooling; no work without a command."""
    
    import argparse
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import runpy
    import sys
    
    
    def main():
        commands = {"check": "check_patchstg.py", "gpu-check": "check_patchstg_gpu.py",
                    "train": "train_patchstg.py", "evaluate": "evaluate_patchstg.py",
                    "export": "export_patchstg_replay.py"}
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("command", choices=commands)
        args, remaining = parser.parse_known_args()
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
        source_path = str(root / "src")
        sys.path.insert(0, source_path)
        os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = source_path + (os.pathsep + os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] if os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH") else "")
        script = root / "scripts" / commands[args.command]
        sys.argv = [str(script), *remaining]
        runpy.run_path(str(script), run_name="__main__")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

        'architecture.md':'''# PatchSTG architecture and shapes
        
        The integrated PatchSTG combines temporal history encoding with spatial attention.
        The completed SD configuration has five blocks, one attention head per operation,
        width 192, and 2,284,844 trainable parameters. The selected checkpoint is epoch 50.
        
        ## Forward path
        
        ```text
        12-step normalized flow + historical input calendar
                                 ↓
        Temporal signal projection + learned sensor/calendar embeddings
                                 ↓
        Gather/pad original sensors into spatial patches
                                 ↓
        Within-patch depth attention + across-patch breadth attention (five blocks)
                                 ↓
        Restore original 716-sensor ordering
                                 ↓
        Projection to 12 normalized forecasts → inverse scale for loss/metrics
        ```
        
        | Stage | Shape |
        | --- | --- |
        | Traffic | `(B,12,716,1)` |
        | Shared calendar (slot, weekday) | `(B,12,2)` |
        | Expanded calendar | `(B,12,716,2)` |
        | Temporal projection + embeddings | `(B,1,716,192)` |
        | Padded patch grid | `(B,1,16,64,192)` |
        | Restored representations | `(B,1,716,192)` |
        | Normalized forecast | `(B,12,716,1)` |
        
        The one-temporal-patch SD path uses history and horizon 12. This implementation
        does not claim support for arbitrary temporal patching or unequal horizons.
        
        ## Embedding components
        
        Signal width 64 + sensor/node width 64 + slot width 32 + weekday width 32 = 192.
        The temporal Conv2d consumes traffic and normalized calendar scalars across the
        12 historical positions. The last input step indexes the calendar embedding
        vectors; node embeddings identify sensors. No future traffic or target calendar
        is supplied by this path.
        
        ## Attention block
        
        Depth attention operates over the 64 positions within each patch. Breadth
        attention operates over the 16 patches at a corresponding within-patch position.
        Their combination permits exchange across the network without one full
        716-by-716 attention operation at every stage.
        
        Each block uses pre-LayerNorm, learned Q/K/V and output projections, scaled dot
        products and softmax, residual additions, and GELU feed-forward layers with width
        ratio one. Dropout is 0.1 at the recorded attention/projection/MLP positions.
        
        Padding positions duplicate selected sensors for computation; restoration
        recovers originals and avoids adding duplicate forecast targets.
        
        ## Method sources and adaptations
        
        Reviewed paper: [PatchSTG v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09972v2).
        Reference code commit: [8b298b2](https://github.com/LMissher/PatchSTG/tree/8b298b230227a304a082e05241c69dca3740a73d).
        The SD code configuration, rather than every paper hyperparameter, defines this
        adaptation. Explicit PyTorch attention replaces timm, and numerical full-upstream
        checkpoint parity has not been established. See [implementation](patchstg_implementation.md).
        ''',
        'spatial_preparation.md':'''# Spatial preparation: training similarity, patches and restoration
        
        Source: [spatial.py](../../src/traffic_benchmark/data/spatial.py).
        Saved maps: [spatial_maps.npz](../../runs/patchstg_sd_seed2023_50ep/spatial_maps.npz).
        
        ## Similarity from training observations only
        
        `training_similarity` requires traffic/scaler statistics for precisely the
        training interval `[0,21024)`. It normalizes training readings with the global
        training mean/std, divides them into full 288-frame segments, averages the
        aligned segment profiles, and calculates cosine similarity between sensors.
        An exponential transform of standardized cosine scores provides padding scores.
        Zero-norm profiles use zero cosine; degenerate cosine variance raises an error.
        
        There are exactly 73 full segments. At the assumed SD cadence, 288 positions
        span three days. This preserves the reviewed code convention; it is not a
        96-slot daily-profile correction or a road-distance adjacency graph.
        
        ## Coordinate partitions and padding
        
        Balanced recursive splits alternate latitude/longitude. Leaf depth 9 produces
        512 leaves with capacity two; 716 sensors require up to 1,024 padded positions.
        Similarity selects padding candidates, and a merge factor of 32 produces
        16 patches of 64 positions. Stable sensor-index tie breaking specifies cases
        that otherwise depend on sort behavior.
        
        The map constructor checks coordinates, similarity dimensions, nonnegative
        scores, and compatible patch settings. Padded duplicates supply representations
        for computation; they are not additional observed sensors or scored targets.
        
        ## Gather and restore
        
        `gather` says which original sensor fills each padded position. `restore` says
        where each original sensor is recovered from that layout. The invariant is:
        
        ```python
        gather[restore] == np.arange(716)
        ```
        
        Every original sensor has exactly one restoration position. Model buffers store
        these maps, move with the device, and are verified before loading checkpoint
        weights that would otherwise overwrite them.
        
        ## Cache identity
        
        Cache metadata includes source hashes, scaler, training boundary, segment and
        partition settings, tie policy, code/version identity and payload checksum.
        Mismatched/corrupt caches fail instead of silently rebuilding a different graph.
        This verifies artifact identity, not independent metadata-column alignment.
        
        Integration loaded and validated the saved maps without reconstructing them or
        performing model inference. The existing maps and scores are reused unchanged.
        ''',
        'patchstg_implementation.md':'''# PatchSTG implementation and integration
        
        Source modules are included under [traffic_benchmark](../../src/traffic_benchmark/__init__.py).
        The model, data preparation, training kernels, metrics and checkpoint utilities
        retain their measured-run code bytes. The model namespace exports PatchSTG only;
        BigST is outside the active scope.
        
        ## Model components
        
        [patchstg.py](../../src/traffic_benchmark/models/patchstg.py) defines:
        
        - `PatchSTGConfig`: fixed SD dimensions, embedding widths, five layers, dropout.
        - `SpatialAttention`: one-head Q/K/V projection, scaled softmax attention and output.
        - `FeedForward`: linear → GELU → dropout → linear → dropout, ratio one.
        - `DualAttentionBlock`: depth within patches, breadth across patches, pre-normalization
          and residual updates.
        - `PatchSTG`: validate traffic/calendar, encode history/context, gather, process,
          restore and decode normalized forecasts.
        
        The calendar may be shared `(B,12,2)` or expanded `(B,12,716,2)`, with int64
        slot/weekday values. Traffic must be finite float32 normalized flow on the same
        device as model/calendar. The caller inverse-transforms predictions for scoring.
        
        ## Recorded checks and current integration checks
        
        The included tests cover maps, training-only preprocessing, attention axes and
        numerics, gradients, cache/checkpoint integrity, training/resume, masks and replay.
        Their recorded diagnostic reports are included. Integration itself verified
        copied hashes and saved checkpoint/report/map identities without rerunning
        PatchSTG training, test scoring or forward inference.
        
        The completed full-width CPU diagnostic recorded 16×64 padded positions and
        finite backward/reload behavior. Those were implementation checks, not forecast
        accuracy claims. The actual saved test result is documented separately.
        
        ## Faithfulness and license
        
        This is a code-aligned shared-protocol adaptation. It substitutes explicit

        ''',

    # Traffic forecasting: contextual LSTM versus PatchSTG
    
    Course project using processed SD traffic observations. The selected contextual
    LSTM has two layers, 256 hidden units, calendar/sensor embeddings, and 848,644
    parameters. It was selected at epoch 37 using validation MAE 15.0656 from the
    two completed 50-epoch candidates. The unfinished 384-unit run is deferred.
    
    ## Project layout
    
    ```text
    README.md                 Start here
    guide.md                  Step-by-step reading path
    src/traffic_prediction/   Data, models, metrics, training and evaluation code
    scripts/                  Runnable commands
    requirements.txt          Direct Python dependencies
    docs/                     Concept guides and implementation walkthroughs
    reports/                  Audit, experiment decisions and recorded checks
    runs/                     Current candidate checkpoints and generated final results
    data/raw/largest_sd/      Local traffic array and metadata
    reproducibility/          Original source snapshots and historical reference evidence
    temp/                    Archived notes, scripts, logs and superseded experiments
    ```
    
    Nothing was deleted during cleanup. `temp/` is not part of the main submission
    narrative; it keeps earlier educational work recoverable. Keep `reproducibility/`:
    existing checkpoints reference original source hashes, and the selected evaluator
    checks them against those exact archived bytes. Current execution source hashes
    are separately recorded in the new evaluation report.
    
    ## Run the selected evaluation and comparison
    
    Use the existing environment from the project root:
    
    ```bash
    conda activate pml
    python -u scripts/finalize_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output-dir runs/final_comparison_v1
    ```
    
    The output directory must be new. This checks the selected checkpoint, reproduces
    validation, scores frozen test predictions, and writes:
    
    - `PROJECT_REPORT.md`: comparison, interpretation, and limitations.
    - `report.json`, `selection.json`, `comparison.json`: machine-readable evidence.
    - Learning curves, forecast-lead curves, and a sensor-error distribution.
    
    Final contextual test scoring is complete: MAE **18.1696**, RMSE **31.9485**,
    MAPE **12.0646%**. Read [the final report](runs/final_comparison_v1/PROJECT_REPORT.md).
    Do not rerun into the existing output directory. PatchSTG is integrated with its source, tests, configurations and saved experiment.
    The comparison reuses its existing measured run without retraining or reevaluation.
    
    For another machine, requirements.txt lists direct dependencies; recorded run
    reports supply the actual experiment versions. A compatible CUDA-enabled PyTorch
    environment is needed for the GPU command. No dependencies were installed or
    changed during this cleanup.
    
    ## Checks and learning
    
    ```bash
    python scripts/check_context_training.py
    python scripts/inspect_data.py
    ```
    
    The first is a synthetic training/validation/resume check. The second runs the
    data walkthrough and baseline validation; neither starts a long training suite.
    
    For GPU feasibility on a new report path:
    
    ```bash
    python scripts/check_context_lstm.py --device cuda --output reports/gpu_probe_repeat.json
    ```
    
    Start learning with [guide.md](guide.md), then use [the documentation index](docs/README.md).
    See [cleanup notes](docs/project_structure.md) for moved files and reproduction details.
    
    ## Submission notes
    
    Keep source, scripts, documentation, reports and reproducibility records together.
    Raw data and model artifacts are local assets; include them only if required by
    the course submission rules. Reproducing evaluation needs the selected candidate
    checkpoints/reports and the original data files at the documented paths. Do not
    claim a source-only submission can execute inference without those assets.
    
    Exclude `temp/`, Python caches and live logs from the submission archive unless
    the instructor requests development history. No archive has been published or
    submitted automatically.
    # Project goal and implemented architecture
    
    The course project applies a method learned in class to practical traffic
    forecasting, then analyzes performance beyond one overall accuracy number.
    The professor recommended an LSTM main model alongside PatchSTG and simple
    baselines. BigST is deferred.
    
    We reuse the previous project's processed SD data: 35,040 assumed 15-minute
    steps at 716 sensors, one traffic-flow channel. Dataset copies match originals.
    The new project rebuilds understandable data handling, baselines, LSTMs, checks,
    training, resume, and frozen evaluation rather than blindly copying everything.
    
    ## Execution map
    
    ```text
    data/raw/largest_sd/flowsd.npz
                  ↓
    data_pipeline.py: split → training scaler → windows → Dataset
                  ↓
    PyTorch DataLoader batches
                  ↓
      ┌─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
      │ TrafficLSTM             │ ContextLSTM                  │
      │ traffic-only, 1 layer    │ traffic + calendar + sensor  │
      │ hidden width 32         │ 2 layers, widths 128/256/384  │
      └─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
                  ↓
    original-unit masked loss → Adam updates (training only)
                  ↓
    full frozen validation → best checkpoint selection
                  ↓
    frozen test assessment after choices are fixed
    ```
    
    Baselines bypass neural training: persistence repeats the latest reading;
    seasonal average fits nonzero training calendar/sensor means.
    The audit separately checks data/metadata and produces training-only plots.
    
    ## What has and has not been built here
    
    All 15 root Python files have dedicated [walkthroughs](README.md).
    The small LSTM completed 50 epochs and test evaluation. The contextual suite
    trains three predefined capacities with validation-only selection; status is
    recorded in [results](results_and_status.md). PatchSTG is integrated with model code, spatial preparation, training/evaluation
    tools, tests, saved checkpoints, measured reports and replay artifacts. No dashboard has been built here.
    
    Contextual candidate test scoring, a final selected contextual test result,
    formal uncertainty estimates, spatial ablations, and controlled cross-model
    runtime benchmarks are not yet implemented/completed in this new study.
    
    The user's learning workflow remains: explain significant changes before

    experiments. No source/checkpoint files were changed to produce these docs.

    """Refresh comparison documents/figures from saved scores; execute no models."""
    
    import argparse
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    import sys
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
    
    from traffic_prediction.finalize_context_lstm import build_comparison
    from traffic_prediction.train_lstm import sha256
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("--results-dir", type=Path, default=ROOT / "runs/final_comparison_v1")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        report = args.results_dir / "report.json"
        original_hash = sha256(report)
        result = json.loads(report.read_text())
        selection = json.loads((args.results_dir / "selection.json").read_text())
        if result["status"] != "complete" or not result["checkpoint_unchanged"]:
            raise ValueError("A completed frozen LSTM evaluation is required.")
        build_comparison(args.results_dir, selection, result, ROOT, ROOT)
        if sha256(report) != original_hash:
            raise RuntimeError("Measured LSTM evaluation report changed.")
        provenance = {"mode": "report/figure refresh from existing completed scores; no training or inference",

    # Spatial patches and sensor index maps
    
    PatchSTG organizes sensor representations into groups so it can exchange spatial
    information using smaller attention operations. This grouping rearranges sensors;
    it does not average each patch into one token or change which sensors are targets.
    
    Coordinate-based recursive splits produce small leaves. Training-derived traffic
    similarity chooses padding positions, then leaves are merged into equal-sized
    patches. For this SD configuration there are 16 patches of 64 positions:
    1,024 computational positions for 716 original sensors.
    
    `gather` maps padded positions to original sensors. `restore` chooses the one
    canonical position for each original sensor. The key invariant is
    `gather[restore] == arange(716)`. Without restoration, predictions can be paired
    with the wrong sensor targets or padded duplicates can incorrectly affect scores.
    
    Similarity is learned from the training interval only. Coordinates are metadata,
    not future traffic. Neither validates the assumed row-to-column pairing by itself.
    The saved maps preserve exact preprocessing used by the trained checkpoint.
    
    Read [spatial preparation](../patchstg/spatial_preparation.md) and
    [the source](../../src/traffic_benchmark/data/spatial.py). The project reuses its
    saved maps; there is no need to rebuild them for the completed comparison.
    Add: /mnt/c/Users/SH Emon/Desktop/Projects/Traffic Prediction PML/docs/concepts/20_spatial_attention.md
    # Spatial attention in PatchSTG
    
    Attention calculates a weighted combination of representations. Learned linear
    projections create queries Q, keys K, and values V. One-head scaled attention is:
    
    ```text
    weights = softmax(Q Kᵀ / sqrt(width))
    output  = weights V
    ```
    
    Queries and keys determine relative weights; values supply mixed information.
    These are learned representations, not necessarily physical road connectivity.
    Weights change with the input. The output projection, normalization, residual
    connections and feed-forward layers are also trainable parts of the block.
    
    PatchSTG applies depth attention among 64 positions within each patch, then
    breadth attention among 16 patches at matching positions. Repeated blocks permit
    information exchange without a single full sensor-pair matrix at every stage.
    The one temporal patch has already encoded the 12 input readings.
    
    Our contextual LSTM shares weights but processes sensor sequences independently.
    PatchSTG mixes sensor representations; that is a functional difference, not a
    guarantee of better accuracy. Capacity, context, optimizer and preprocessing
    also differ, so an accuracy gap does not isolate attention as its cause.
    
    Read [architecture](../patchstg/architecture.md) and
    [model source](../../src/traffic_benchmark/models/patchstg.py), focusing on
    SpatialAttention and DualAttentionBlock before the complete forward method.

    """Verify integrated saved PatchSTG artifacts without constructing/running a model."""
    
    import argparse
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    import sys
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
    
    import torch
    from traffic_benchmark.data import GlobalStandardScaler
    from traffic_benchmark.data.spatial import load_spatial_maps
    from traffic_benchmark.evaluation.checkpoint import file_sha256, validate_checkpoint
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=ROOT / "reports/patchstg_integration.json")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        run = ROOT / "runs/patchstg_sd_seed2023_50ep"
        report = json.loads((run / "report.json").read_text())
        test = json.loads((ROOT / "reports/patchstg_sd_seed2023_test_v1.json").read_text())
        checkpoint = torch.load(run / "best.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        hashes = {name: file_sha256(ROOT / "data/raw/largest_sd" / name)
                  for name in ("flowsd.npz", "sd_meta.csv")}
        # validate_checkpoint checks recorded source paths relative to project root.
        import os
        previous_cwd = Path.cwd()
        try:
            os.chdir(ROOT)
            identity = validate_checkpoint(checkpoint, report, hashes, report["identity"]["splits"],
                                           GlobalStandardScaler(**report["identity"]["scaler"]))
            maps = load_spatial_maps(run / "spatial_maps.npz", identity["spatial"])
        finally:
            os.chdir(previous_cwd)
        if [e["epoch"] for e in report["history"]] != list(range(1, 51)):
            raise ValueError("Incomplete training history.")
        if file_sha256(run / "best.pt") != test["checkpoint"]["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Selected checkpoint differs from saved test evaluation.")
        if file_sha256(run / "report.json") != test["training_report_sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Full training report differs from saved test evaluation.")
        if file_sha256(run / "spatial_maps.npz") != test["spatial_maps_sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Spatial maps differ from saved test evaluation.")
        if test["source_hashes"] != hashes or test["checkpoint"]["epoch"] != checkpoint["epoch"]:
            raise ValueError("Saved test data/epoch identity differs.")
        for name, expected in (("gather_indices", maps.gather), ("restore_indices", maps.restore)):
            if checkpoint["model"][name].tolist() != expected.tolist():
                raise ValueError("Saved model spatial buffers differ.")
        if any(not torch.isfinite(v).all() for v in checkpoint["model"].values()):
            raise ValueError("Saved model state contains nonfinite values.")
        result = {"status": "verified", "selected_epoch": checkpoint["epoch"], "completed_epochs": 50,
                  "spatial_patches": maps.patch_count, "patch_size": maps.patch_size,
                  "checkpoint_sha256": file_sha256(run / "best.pt"),
                  "training_report_sha256": file_sha256(run / "report.json"),
                  "data_sha256": hashes, "test": test["results"]["test"]["overall_pooled"],
                  "execution": "hash/metadata/tensor/map checks only; no model construction, forward, training or evaluation",
                  "test_metrics_source": "integrated completed saved run; unchanged"}
        if args.output.exists():
            raise FileExistsError("Integration check output exists; choose a new --output path.")
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()
